; UpdateAudioVoices: Consume one queued sound, resolve voice priority and update seven 32-byte voice records. Active voices advance timing and decode new stream events before updating APU registers.

; UpdateOneVoice: X selects a voice. Advance its event timer, compute pitch and envelope, then write changed period/volume values. Voice flags select hardware channel and suppress writes when another voice owns it.

; InterpolateVoicePitch: When slide flag $20 is set, scale the signed difference between target and base period by elapsed/duration. Otherwise copy base period directly. Uses shared audio arithmetic scratch.
; AdvanceVoiceEnvelope: Use the global audio tick and envelope selector to derive the low-nibble output volume. Packed envelope nibbles can restart or hold the cursor.
; ContinueVoiceEnvelope: Rejoin the envelope decoder after increasing base volume toward its target.
; DecodeEnvelopeNibble: A zero envelope selector uses fixed volume. Otherwise a packed nibble stream adjusts base volume and advances the envelope cursor; special nibble values control hold/restart.
; ContinuePackedEnvelope: Repeat packed-nibble decoding at the current envelope cursor.
; ResolveVoicePriority: Copy the active high-priority voice sign bit into the paired lower-priority voice suppression flag, preserving its other flags.
; SetVoiceSuppression: A sign bit controls bit $04 of the flags supplied in Y; return the modified flags in A.
; MultiplyAudioBytes: Shift/add multiplication of audio scratch $eb and $ec into the 16-bit result $ee/$ef; preserves Y.
; DivideAudioWord: Restoring division of $ec:$eb by $ed over sixteen bit steps. Quotient low byte is returned in $ee; callers use this to scale pitch slides.
; DispatchAudioCommand: High stream bytes select an indirect command handler through a two-byte pointer table. Stream cursor Y and voice index are shared with handlers.

; DecodeVoiceEvent: Read the voice stream pointer. Bytes below $e0 encode note/rest, optional slide target and duration; higher bytes invoke commands. Store advanced pointer and reset elapsed/envelope cursors.
; StoreVoiceSlideTargetHigh: Fetch the high period byte from the note table and retain the channel scratch index for the common event tail.
; CallAudioCommandPointer: Indirect tail call through the pointer in audio scratch $eb/$ec.
; Thirty-two CPU handler words selected by stream opcode AND $1f.
; SetVoiceControlParameter: Copy one stream operand into voice field two. Its exact sound-level interpretation remains unresolved.
; SetVoiceBaseVolume: Read the command operand into the voice base-volume field; the caller advances the stream cursor.
; SetVoiceEnvelopeSelector: Install the stream-selected envelope index and return to common command advancement.
; SetVoiceParameter6: Set voice parameter six from one stream operand. Its sound-level use remains unresolved.
; SetVoiceFlagsAndVolumeTarget: OR stream flag bits into voice state, set the target volume, and restart the shared envelope tick.
; AddVoiceTranspose: Add the signed stream operand to the per-voice transposition byte, wrapping at eight bits.
; RepeatAudioPhrase: Maintain a per-voice indexed repeat counter. Until it expires, replace the stream pointer with a two-byte operand and return cursor $ff so common advancement restarts correctly.
; EnableVoiceSlide: Set the pitch interpolation flag and back up the cursor because this command has no operand.
; AudioDebugBreak: Back up the stream cursor and execute BRK. IRQ RTI resumes after the separate signature byte; it does not execute that byte as RTS.
; BRK signature byte $60 is skipped by stacked PC+2 and IRQ RTI; this is Data, not a standalone return routine.
; DisableVoiceSlide: Clear pitch-slide flag $20 and back up Y because this command has no operand.
; SetVoiceSweepCache: Use the voice channel low bits to select one of the sweep caches, store the operand, and restore the voice index.
; SetVoiceParameter28: Store the stream operand in voice offset $18. Its later game-level meaning is unresolved.
; SuppressVoiceRegisterWrites: Set flag $02 so the voice advances without writing hardware registers; no stream operand.
; ResumeVoiceRegisterWrites: Clear flag $02 and compensate the no-operand command cursor.
; EnableRawVoicePeriod: Enable raw period encoding for subsequent stream events; this flag distinguishes periods from note-table indices.
; DisableRawVoicePeriod: Clear raw-period flag $08 so subsequent events again use note-table encoding.
; CallAudioPhrase: Save the return stream address on the voice-local descending two-byte stack and load a phrase pointer. The command stream, not the CPU stack, controls nesting.
; Return from an audio phrase: restore the saved stream pointer and pop two voice-local stack bytes.
; PopSoundQueue: If the queue is nonempty, take its first command, shift sixteen following bytes down and decrement its count.
; DispatchQueuedSound: Commands $81 through $a1 select paired descriptor and handler pointers. Invalid commands reset audio; $80 leaves the engine idle.
; ResetInvalidSound: Clear priority and APU enables, mark the pending command idle, then clear voice state.
; ClearAudioVoices: Clear seven voice flags and sweep caches, set muted control defaults, and enable the four ordinary APU channels.
; MuteAudioRegisters: Write cached silent register defaults without clearing every voice record. Entry lies within the reset helper.
; Thirty-three descriptor pointers for validated commands $81..$a1. Dispatcher uses a base-minus-two indexed alias.
; Thirty-three initialization-handler pointers paired with the command descriptors.
; StartPrimarySound: Clear the engine, then select the voice-record destination at $0570 before initializing a sound descriptor.
; Lower-priority voice start: leave current voices intact while priority bit $80 is set.
; StartVoiceAt0550: Use destination $0550 and enter common descriptor initialization.
; StartVoiceAt0510Checked: Gate destination $0510 on the priority latch before starting the sound.
; StartPrioritySound: Mute registers, latch priority bit $80 and suppress existing voices before installing records at $0530.
; StartPrioritySoundAlternate: Mute cached output, latch high priority and clear flag $10 on the six paired voices before joining descriptor initialization.
; StartVoiceAt0530Checked: Skip lower-priority initialization while the priority latch is active.
; StartVoiceAt0530: Select destination $0530 for common descriptor initialization.

; InitializeSoundRecords: Descriptor begins with a record count. Copy nine bytes per voice, initialize timer defaults, clear the remaining record bytes and advance source by nine and destination by $20.
; FinishSoundInitialization: Mark the pending sound command idle and return.

; BeginIncrementalTransfer: Index a pointer list by A, read a signed selector and load two source cursors from a four-byte record. Negative selector disables the transfer; each record lasts fourteen updates.

; Complete bytes, adjacent accepted routines/assets and retained indexed-consumer review support non-code. No specific record layout or original use was established; preserve this generic Data boundary.

; Thirty-three four-byte records, two CPU cursor words each. The first addresses fourteen source glyphs; the second advances a paired transfer destination/cursor. BeginIncrementalTransfer loads both and sets fourteen ticks.
; Thirty-three fixed fourteen-glyph lines selected by four-byte incremental-transfer descriptors. A-Z use $37..$50 and space $5b; other glyphs retain their numeric encoding.
; QueueIncrementalTransfer: Queue a type-7 transfer with two advancing word cursors and a one-byte count. After fourteen iterations advance the selector list.

; QuantizeDecimalDisplay: Temporarily decrement four encoded decimal digits, subtract five repeatedly to select a seven-byte display record, then restore the digits and queue the display operation. Interpretation of this particular display remains tentative.
; LoadDisplayQuantizationRecord: Compute 8*(incoming Y-1) modulo 256, then copy seven bytes from that table offset into $85..$8b. The full natural selector domain is unresolved.
; The consumer uses 8*(incoming Y-1) modulo 256 as its byte index; arbitrary incoming Y is not established as a valid table selector.

; Fourteen eight-byte storage records. For an in-range record, LoadDisplayQuantizationRecord copies seven bytes and skips the eighth. The skipped-byte role and full natural selector domain remain unresolved.
; AddFiveDecimalDigits: Add five to four unpacked decimal digits, carrying at ten. These digits use the caller's temporary zero-based representation.
; SubtractFiveDecimalDigits: Subtract five with decimal borrow. Carry is set only when borrowing beyond the highest digit; otherwise clear.
; FillUiNametable: Set PPU address $2000 and fill runs using a low counter plus a signed high counter. Rendering must already permit direct PPU access.

; LoadDirectNametableRuns: Read the fixed source at $b46d as destination-word/run records and write PPU bytes directly. The destination-derived $e3 marker terminates. Rendering must permit direct writes.
